designer: Klipper community + multiple GitHub forks (e.g., 3DChirality, klipper-extruder-pump variants)
license_notes: Klipper firmware GPL-3.0; host Python GPL-3.0; hardware STL CC-BY-SA-4.0 across upstream forks.
purpose: Single- or multi-channel syringe pump driven by Klipper firmware on commodity 3D-printer control boards (BTT SKR, Duet 3, FYSETC). Treats the syringe plunger as a printer extruder, exposing G-code (E moves at user-configurable steps/uL) for protocol scripting.

hardware_artifacts.format: Klipper config + STL printer-derivative pump frames

bill_of_materials.part: T8 lead screw 200 mm + brass nut

validated_performance: TMC2209-driven NEMA 17 with 256x microstepping yields ~0.05 uL resolution on a 10 mL syringe at 8 mm/rev T8. Flow accuracy ~1.5% at 50 uL/min, limited by syringe compliance, not motor.
sources: Various community forks for microfluidic use under github.com/topics/klipper-pump
notes: Real working OSS — Klipper firmware itself is mature and proven. Catalog entry consolidates the pattern of using Klipper as a syringe-pump controller; needs a canonical KiCad/STL deposit of a microfluidic-specific pump frame to clear the hardware bar.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder pending community deposit)
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT; per-cartesian frame CC-BY-SA-4.0.
purpose: Open cartesian-arm pipetting platform analog to the Andrew Alliance Andrew+ robot. Picks Gilson-style air-displacement pipettes off a parking dock and executes liquid-handling protocols on a 96/384-well deck.
sources: Andrew Alliance product literature (commercial reference, closed)
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted entry. Commercial Andrew+ is closed source; this catalog slot is reserved for an open reimplementation. Distinguishing capability vs. Opentrons OT-2: the Andrew+ paradigm uses standard handheld Gilson pipettes parked on the deck (so consumables and tips are off-the-shelf), instead of custom proprietary pipette heads. A commons-grade entry needs a working open cartesian arm + pipette grip mechanism.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (host bridge) + CETONI (commercial pump, open API)
license_notes: Host bridge MIT (this entry); CETONI QmixSDK is closed but exposes a documented binary interface; community Python wrappers (e.g., PyQmixSDK) are MIT.
purpose: Open Rust + Python host-side controller and protocol bridge for the commercial CETONI neMESYS / Nemesys-S syringe-pump modules. Re-exposes QmixSDK functionality through a uniform JSON-RPC API so neMESYS pumps can be scripted alongside fully open pumps in the same protocol runner.

hardware_artifacts.format: USB CAN-bus interface adapter PCB (KiCad placeholder)

validated_performance: Per CETONI neMESYS spec: flow rate 0.5 nL/min to 200 mL/min, dosing accuracy < 0.25%, pressure resilience to 5 bar.
notes: Hybrid entry: hardware is commercial closed; the contribution is the open bridge so neMESYS pumps coexist in open protocols. Useful for groups that already own neMESYS hardware. CC0 cataloging only — no claim on CETONI IP.

canonical_name: Open Bartels mp6 micropump driver board
designer: Free Microfluidics Project + community (Bartels Mikrotechnik publishes evaluation schematics)
license_notes: Driver-board hardware CERN-OHL-P (this entry); the mp6 piezo pump itself is a commercial component.
purpose: Open KiCad driver board for the Bartels mp6 piezoelectric micropump. Generates the 250 V peak-to-peak square-wave drive at 5-300 Hz required by the mp6, with USB control and on-board flow setpoint feedback via a downstream Sensirion liquid flow sensor.

hardware_artifacts.format: KiCad project (placeholder); mp6-OEM driver schematic from Bartels app note as reference

bill_of_materials.part: H-bridge for piezo (4x MOSFET high-side / low-side driver)

validated_performance: Per Bartels mp6 datasheet: free-flow up to 7 mL/min water, back pressure up to 600 mbar at 100 Hz. Driver target: deliver datasheet performance ±5% with closed-loop SLF3S-0600F feedback.
notes: Bartels publishes the mp6-OEM evaluation driver schematic; multiple open community redraws exist on GitHub (search 'mp6 driver kicad'). Catalog entry is the canonical CERN-OHL-P consolidation.

designer: Community reverse-engineering (multiple GitHub forks)
license_notes: Bridge firmware MIT (this entry); the Watson-Marlow pumps themselves are commercial closed.
purpose: Open RS-485 / Modbus bridge to drive Watson-Marlow 120-series and 320-series peristaltic pumps from a host computer. Implements the publicly-documented and partially community-reverse-engineered RS-485 control protocol.
validated_performance: Per Watson-Marlow 120U spec: 0.0008-12 mL/min in 0.0001 mL/min increments with appropriate tubing; pressure to 2 bar.
sources: Community forum threads on RS-485 protocol reverse-engineering
notes: Hybrid entry: pump commercial, bridge open. Catalog entry exists so groups owning Watson-Marlow units can put them under the same protocol runner as fully open pumps. The reverse-engineered Modbus map should be published in docs/ as a CC0 reference table.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder) + Cornell academic prior art
license_notes: Driver hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT; chip geometry CC0 in this catalog.
purpose: Drive board for resonant acoustically-actuated bubble micropumps (Cornell-style trapped-bubble streaming pumps). Generates 1-100 kHz sinusoidal piezo drive at 10-40 V peak-to-peak with frequency sweep for bubble-resonance lock-in.

firmware_artifacts.language: Rust embassy on STM32G4 (DAC + analog peak-detect)

validated_performance: Target: 50-500 uL/min through 100 um wide PDMS channel with single 60 um trapped bubble at f-resonance, per Cornell-style streaming-pump literature (Marmottant / Ahmed).
publication_citation: Tovar AR, Lee AP. Lateral cavity acoustic transducer. Lab Chip 2009;9:41-43.
sources: Hashmi et al. Lab Chip 2012 (oscillating bubble micropump)
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted entry — academic prior art is solid but no canonical OSS deposit exists for the driver electronics. Listed as scaffold for a contributor to deposit a working driver + characterized chip.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder); inspired by community Elveflow protocol reverse-engineering threads
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT; protocol reverse-engineering CC0.
purpose: Four-channel ±2 bar pressure / vacuum controller as an open replacement for the Elveflow OB1. Two channels of pressure (0 to +2 bar), two channels of pressure or vacuum (-0.9 to +2 bar), per-channel proportional valves with 1 mbar resolution.
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted entry. Distinct from the existing dual-channel-pressure-controller-stm32 by being four-channel with two vacuum-capable lines, targeting full OB1 feature parity. Commercial OB1 is ~$8k; BOM target ~$1.9k.

canonical_name: Open Fluigent MFCS / Aria protocol bridge
designer: Community + Free Microfluidics Project bridge
license_notes: Bridge MIT; Fluigent SDK (fgt_SDK / Fluigent_SDK_for_Python) is closed binary but documented; MFCS USB protocol partially community-described.
purpose: Open Rust + Python bridge for Fluigent MFCS-EZ, Flow EZ, and Aria pressure controllers, exposing a uniform JSON-RPC API. Lets Fluigent-equipped labs script their hardware in the same protocol runner as fully open pressure controllers.

hardware_artifacts.format: USB cable adapter, no PCB needed

validated_performance: Per Fluigent MFCS-EZ spec: 0-1000 mbar, 0.1 mbar resolution, 200 ms response time.
notes: Hybrid entry. The bridge is the contribution; the hardware is commercial. Provides interoperability for groups bridging open and commercial pressure-controller fleets.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder); descended from Brower / Quake group on/off solenoid PWM pressure schemes
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT.
purpose: Low-cost 8-channel air-over-liquid pressure controller using on/off solenoids in PWM mode against a fixed regulated supply, with closed-loop pressure feedback for ~10 mbar resolution. Suitable for PDMS chip perfusion at modest precision.

firmware_artifacts.language: Arduino-C++ (atmega2560) or Rust embassy on RP2040

validated_performance: Target: 0-1000 mbar, ~10 mbar PID-stabilized resolution, ~50 ms response time. Suitable for steady perfusion; not for fast pressure transients.
sources: Brower et al. HardwareX 2018 (Quake group pressure rig)
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted entry. Cheaper / lower-resolution alternative to the proportional-regulator open-OB1-clone entry. Many lab groups have built variants; canonical KiCad + characterization deposit needed.

canonical_name: Open mass flow controller (MFC) bridge board
designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder)
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT.
purpose: Bridge board exposing a uniform USB / Modbus / CAN interface to commercial mass flow controllers from Bronkhorst, MKS, and Sensirion. Provides 0-5 V analog setpoint and readback per MFC plus per-vendor digital protocol passthrough (Bronkhorst FLOW-BUS, MKS RS-232, Sensirion SHDLC).
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted bridge board so commercial MFCs (gas-side, common in droplet microfluidics for nitrogen / synthetic air) can plug into the same protocol stack as the open pressure controllers.

designer: Sci-Bots / DropBot / Wheeler group community fork (microdrop-3)
license_notes: MicroDrop GUI BSD-3-Clause; DropBot firmware MIT; PCB CERN-OHL-P.
purpose: Open EWOD digital-microfluidics control platform paired with the DropBot v3/v4 high-voltage driver. Provides protocol scripting (drop merge, split, transport) and impedance-feedback drop detection on 120-electrode EWOD chips.

hardware_artifacts.format: KiCad project for DropBot v3/v4 board

validated_performance: Per DropBot v3 spec: drive voltage 0-300 V RMS at 100 Hz to 10 kHz, drop transport at 1-10 mm/s on Cytop-coated chips, impedance-feedback drop detection at SNR > 20 dB.
publication_citation: Fobel R, Fobel C, Wheeler AR. DropBot: An open-source digital microfluidic control system. Appl Phys Lett 2013;102:193513.
notes: Real working OSS — DropBot + MicroDrop is the most mature open EWOD stack. Distinct from the open-ewod-driver-dropbot-derivative entry, which is a stub for a forward port; this entry catalogs the actual upstream Sci-Bots tooling.

canonical_name: Open-Drop EWOD platform (NUS Intelligent Robotics Group)
designer: NUS Intelligent Robotics Group / GaudiLabs OpenDrop project (Urs Gaudenz)
license_notes: Hardware CC-BY-SA-4.0; firmware GPL-3.0 per upstream OpenDrop.
purpose: Compact, accessible EWOD platform with 8x14 = 112-electrode array, designed for educational and citizen-science use. Driven by a single PCB with on-board high-voltage AC generation and ESP32 wireless control.
validated_performance: Per OpenDrop documentation: 200 V peak square-wave drive at 1 kHz, drop transport on 112-electrode array, hand-pipetted-droplet manipulation 1-5 uL drops.
notes: Real working OSS — GaudiLabs OpenDrop is well-documented and citable. Catalog entry consolidates v3 and v4. Distinct lineage from DropBot/MicroDrop (Wheeler group); listed separately because hardware and firmware diverge.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder); descended from Stanford Foundry / Quake group practice
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT; mechanical CC0.
purpose: 16- to 48-channel pneumatic valve manifold rack for Quake-style PDMS membrane valves. Each channel is a 3-way solenoid switching between 30 psi pressurized water/air and atmosphere, driven by a high-side MOSFET array under USB control with sub-10 ms switching.
validated_performance: Target: < 8 ms switching time, supply pressure 0-30 psi, leak rate < 0.1 mbar/min per channel. Sized for the standard Quake-valve PDMS device class (Unger et al. Science 2000).
publication_citation: Unger MA et al. Monolithic microfabricated valves and pumps by multilayer soft lithography. Science 2000;288:113.
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted entry. The existing open-pneumatic-valve-bank-controller and open-multiplexed-valve-controller-256 cover the broader category; this entry is specifically the Stanford-Foundry-style 19-inch rack form factor most academic groups want as a starting point.

designer: Multiple lineages (JUAMI / IO Rodeo MiniStat / EmStat-clone community)
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT; host software MIT.
purpose: Single-channel ±2.5 V potentiostat with cyclic voltammetry, chronoamperometry, and EIS modes. ±10 mA current range with 1 nA resolution. KiCad-native open hardware with a USB control link and Python host SDK.
validated_performance: Per IO Rodeo characterization: ±2.5 V potential, ±10 mA current, 1 nA resolution, CV scan rate 1 mV/s to 1 V/s, EIS 0.01 Hz to 100 kHz.
publication_citation: Cordova-Huaman AV et al. Low-cost smartphone-controlled potentiostat. HardwareX 2019;6:e00085 (and related JUAMI / Adam Wickenheiser series).
notes: Real working OSS — IO Rodeo potentiostat is a mature reference. Distinct from open-potentiostat-dstat-derivative (DStat lineage); this entry catalogs the IO Rodeo / JUAMI lineage as a separate id.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder); descended from J.M. Pearce open-hardware lab fluorometer designs
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT; mechanical CC0; LED + photodiode positioning per Pearce HardwareX papers.
purpose: Single-cuvette excitation/emission fluorometer at user-selectable LED excitation wavelengths (470, 530, 625 nm) with TIA-amplified photodiode emission detection. Targeted at GFP / fluorescein / Cy5 readout.

firmware_artifacts.language: Arduino-C++ on ATmega328 / Rust embassy on RP2040

validated_performance: Target per Pearce-lab characterization: detection limit ~10 nM fluorescein at 470 nm excitation in standard 1 cm cuvette, dynamic range 4 decades.
publication_citation: Wijnen B, Petersen E, Hunt EJ, Pearce JM. Free and open source automated 3-D microscope. J Microscopy 2016 (and related Pearce-lab HardwareX fluorometer papers).
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted: multiple Pearce-lab and Appropedia community designs exist; this entry is the canonical CERN-OHL-P consolidation pending a community-blessed KiCad deposit.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder); descended from Public Lab Desktop Spectrometry Kit lineage and Hamamatsu mini-spec breakouts
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT; calibration data CC0.
purpose: USB-controlled 350-850 nm CCD spectrometer for absorbance / fluorescence emission scanning, suitable as an open replacement for the Ocean Optics USB2000 in the $2k commercial range.

firmware_artifacts.language: Rust embassy on STM32G4 (CCD readout + serialization)

validated_performance: Per Hamamatsu C12880MA spec: 340-850 nm wavelength range, ~15 nm FWHM, S/N > 300 at 8 ms integration. Open enclosure target: maintain those specs after assembly.
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted. The Hamamatsu C12880MA is the standard low-cost CCD module used in dozens of open-spectrometer GitHub projects; canonical CERN-OHL-P deposit consolidating those into one buildable instrument is the contribution wanted.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder); descended from Ozcan group (UCLA) smartphone fluorescence imaging publications
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware (LED driver micro) MIT; mobile app MIT.
purpose: Smartphone-attachable fluorescence detector for lateral-flow strips and chip wells. Uses phone CMOS as detector, 3D-printed light-tight housing, integrated 470 nm LED excitation, and emission filter. Real-time RGB analysis on phone for quantification.

hardware_artifacts.format: KiCad LED driver + STEP optical housing (placeholder)

validated_performance: Per Ozcan-group lineage of smartphone fluorescence papers: detection limits ~1-10 nM fluorescein-labeled target depending on phone CMOS QE; quantification dynamic range 2-3 decades.
publication_citation: Wei Q, Qi H, Luo W, Tseng D, Ki SJ, Wan Z, Gorocs Z, Bentolila LA, Wu T-T, Sun R, Ozcan A. Fluorescent imaging of single nanoparticles and viruses on a smartphone. ACS Nano 2013;7:9147.
sources: Ozcan group publications (e.g., ACS Nano 2013, Lab Chip 2014, 2016)
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted. The Ozcan lab has published many variants but few open KiCad/STEP deposits. Canonical CC0 consolidation invites a contributor to release a working clip-on with phone-specific housing variants for common modern handsets.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder); descended from open lock-in amplifier projects (e.g., Stanford SR830 reverse-engineering, OpenLockIn)
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT.
purpose: Single-channel photodiode TIA + digital lock-in amplifier for chopped-LED fluorescence in microfluidic flow cells. Supports reference-frequency sweep 100 Hz to 100 kHz, ~120 dB dynamic range with 100 ms time constant.

firmware_artifacts.language: Rust embassy on STM32H7 (CORDIC-based digital lock-in)

validated_performance: Target: 120 dB dynamic range at 100 ms time constant, equivalent input noise ~5 fA/√Hz at 1 kHz; matches commercial Stanford Research SR830 within 10 dB across 1-10 kHz band.
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted. Distinct from existing open-lock-in-amplifier entry by being purpose-built for the photodiode TIA front-end relevant to chopped-LED fluorescence in microfluidic flow cells, rather than the general-purpose lock-in.

designer: OpenFlexure project (Bath / Cambridge, R. Bowman et al.) + community add-on
license_notes: OpenFlexure CERN-OHL-S 2.0 / CC-BY-SA-4.0 mechanical; firmware GPL-3.0; this fluidic add-on inherits OpenFlexure license stack.
purpose: Fluidic-chip mounting plate for OpenFlexure microscope. Replaces the slide stage with a chip carrier for 25x75 mm glass-bonded PDMS chips, with integrated capillary-tubing strain reliefs and warm-stage Peltier mount for live-cell imaging.

bill_of_materials.part: OpenFlexure Microscope Delta v7 base kit

validated_performance: Per OpenFlexure paper: x/y stepping repeatability ~70 nm in normal mode; warm-stage extension target 37 ± 0.3 °C across the chip footprint.
publication_citation: Collins JT, Knapper J, Stirling J, Mduda J, Mkindi C, Mayagaya V, Mwakajinga GA, Nyakyi PT, Sanga VL, Carbery D, White L, Dale S, Lim ZJ, Baumberg JJ, Cicuta P, McDermott S, Vodenicharski B, Bowman R. Robotic microscopy for everyone: the OpenFlexure microscope. Biomed Opt Express 2020;11:2447.
sources: Collins et al. Biomed Opt Express 2020
notes: Real working OSS — OpenFlexure is one of the strongest open-microscope projects. The fluidic add-on is the Free Microfluidics Project's contribution layer; canonical OpenSCAD source pending in the add-on repo.

designer: Free Microfluidics Project (placeholder); descended from community Allcrew / Cambridge Peltier driver designs
license_notes: Hardware CERN-OHL-P; firmware MIT.
purpose: Bidirectional H-bridge Peltier driver board with closed-loop PID temperature control via PT100 / thermistor feedback. ±5 A drive at 12 V, 0.1 °C stability target, USB serial setpoint and telemetry.
validated_performance: Target: 0-60 °C control range with PT100 feedback, ±0.1 °C stability at steady state, 5 °C/s ramp on a 1 cm² aluminum block.
notes: Shape-of-contribution-wanted. Distinct from the existing open-temperature-controller-pid by targeting bidirectional Peltier drive (heat + cool) rather than resistive heater PID. Building block for the open thermal cycler and microfluidic thermostat entries.
